title: Self-Training Agents: Hermes Agent, HF Traces, Skills, MCP & Finetuning  — Merve Noyan, Hugging Face
talk_summary: Merve Noyan of Hugging Face surveys open-model tooling: local coding agents (pi, llama-agent), the Hermes agent, HF Hub 'traces' dataset repos for capturing agent sessions, HF Skills that let coding agents launch training/jobs, and an MCP server exposing Hub models/datasets/spaces/jobs. The one concrete production anecdote is OCR-ing 30,000 papers by prompting an agent to pick a model, write the job script, and launch it on HF infra.

takeaways.technique: Capture agent traces as first-class datasets for later training/eval
takeaways.what_they_do: HF Hub added a 'traces' dataset repo type; you upload session files from known paths and the viewer parses them, and later you can train a model on that data.

takeaways.technique: Packaged 'skills' that wrap CLI/infra operations for agents
takeaways.what_they_do: HF ships installable skills (HF CLI, LLM trainer, dataset viewer, Gradio) so a coding agent can manage repos, launch jobs, and explore datasets through documented commands rather than improvising.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have this thing called the Hugging Face CLI skill, which allows coding agents to manage repositories, run jobs, launch demos

takeaways.technique: Agent does the sizing math, then launches a remote job
takeaways.what_they_do: The agent computes VRAM/instance requirements and cost, asks a couple of clarifying questions, then kicks off a one-off remote job that bills only for uptime.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the agent actually uh, calculates the amount of VRAM required to run fine-tune that model in a given batch size

takeaways.technique: Benchmark-table model selection instead of vibes
takeaways.what_they_do: Uses HF benchmark datasets (SWE-Bench Pro etc.) and inference-provider comparison columns (cheapest/fastest/tool-use) to pick an open model per task.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can actually pick one of the open source models for the agentic use case

takeaways.technique: MCP server exposing search + one-off jobs
takeaways.what_they_do: HF MCP server lets an agent search models/datasets/spaces and invoke hosted apps and one-off jobs directly from the chat client.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we have something called jobs, which allows you to kick off uh, one-off jobs that ends like if it fails or if it succeeds

takeaways.technique: Prompt-driven batch pipeline (pick model, write script, launch job)
takeaways.what_they_do: They OCR'd 30,000 papers by having the agent choose a cheap OCR model, write the processing script, and launch it on HF infra via skills.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we OCR 30 30,000 papers uh using Codex open OCR models and jobs all through prompting
